title: Mask: segment images and inspect the results
description: Load microscope images, choose segmentation settings, preview objects and save masks for measurement.
objectives: Load the microscopy example and identify its intensity channels.
Compare model settings and object-size filters in Live preview.
Run segmentation, inspect its figures and find the merged outputs.
prerequisite: Open Mask and choose Load test data. For your own images, prepare a source folder with consistent filenames and known channel identities. This example uses nucleus channel 0, cell channel 1 and pathogen channel 2, with an additional intensity channel 3.

scenes.narration: From Home, open Mask. Use this module to outline cells, nuclei and pathogens in microscope images. This walkthrough processes two-dimensional images. The Time, three-dimensional and OPS workflows have their own tutorials.

If your images are scattered across folders or named in a way Mask cannot read, click Organize images at the top of Input & Metadata. Give each channel a column, by dropping its folder or by a regex, and check that every row is one complete field. Apply moves the images into one folder with Yokogawa names and points Source at it, with the channels already filled in.

Click Load test data and wait for the microscopy example to load. Check Source before continuing. For your own images, select their folder and confirm that the filenames identify the plate, well, field and channel.

Check the channel assignments against the images. In this example, nucleus intensity is channel zero, cell intensity is channel one, and pathogen intensity is channel two. Channel three is an additional intensity image. Choose only the object types present in your experiment.

Below the inputs, the per-object table holds the settings you choose for each object. Each object is a column, here cell, nucleus and pathogen, and each row asks one question: whether to remove background, the object diameter, the segmentation model, the background level and the signal-to-noise cutoff. Add a filter adds a row that removes objects by a measured property such as area, and Add an organelle adds another object column.
Turn on Live and select a field. Inspect the image and proposed masks together before running the full folder. Try several fields that represent the range of image quality in your experiment.
Open Live settings and choose the model for the object you want to segment. Set the approximate object diameter, then click Run preview.
When the preview finishes, compare the outlines with the image. Look for missed objects and for neighbouring objects joined into one. The status line reports how many objects were found.

Use the minimum-area filter to hide objects smaller than the chosen number of pixels. Increasing it removes small labels from the preview. This filter updates an existing mask result, so you can compare size cutoffs quickly.

Set the minimum area back to zero to bring every object back. If the model splits or joins objects at the wrong scale, change Diameter and run the preview again, checking the boundaries as well as the count. Restore the settings you want before the batch run.

For a quick first run, this recording points Source at centred crops of two example fields; with your own data, turn on Test mode and choose a few test images instead. Keep Plot on, check the per-object diameters and flow thresholds, keep Save on under Quality Control, then click Run.

When the run finishes, the figure list fills with its plots. The last figure draws each object's outlines on its own channel, nuclei, cells and pathogens, and the combined objects on the right. Check small objects, touching cells and missed regions in each figure.

The other figures show each channel and the mask and flow arrays the model produced. The run writes a merged folder with the image intensities and the final object labels, and keeps its plane-layout metadata beside the arrays so Measure can identify each channel and mask. Keep the inputs, settings, masks and quality reports together, then continue to Measure to extract object features and crops.
